title: Coherent evaluation compared with the ordered-cone straightening adjunction
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent functor categories and transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the coherent nerve and space category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and the explicit rigidification $\mathfrak C$, projective simplicial model category $\mathsf D_S$, its cofibrant-fibrant subcategory $\mathsf D_S^{cf}$, right-fibration simplicial category $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ and ordered-cone adjunction $T\dashv U_S$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory $S$; all categories of small objects are formed in a containing universe. Thus $\mathsf D_S$ consists of enriched functors $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$. Its projective weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise, and a superscript $cf$ means projectively cofibrant and projectively fibrant.

Enriched evaluation $(s,P)\mapsto P(s)$, composed with the rigidification unit $S^{\mathrm{op}}\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}})$ and transposed in the $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ variable, defines a comparison
$$\mathsf{ev}_S:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf D_S^{cf})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}).$$
This particular comparison is an equivalence. There is an equivalence
$$\Phi_S:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf{RFib}(S))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$$
and a coherent natural equivalence $\Phi_S N_{\mathrm{hc}}(U_S)\simeq\mathsf{ev}_S$ compatible with the unit and counit of the specified cone adjunction. More explicitly, for every right fibration $q:Y\to S$, every projective trivial cofibration $T_q\to P_q$ with fibrant target gives a cofibrant-fibrant $P_q$ and compatible equivalences
$$\Phi_S(q)\simeq\mathsf{ev}_S(P_q)\simeq m_q,$$
where $m_q:S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ is the coherent fibre-transport functor defined in [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit]. These are equivalences of whole coherent functors. Under the comparison, evaluation at $s$ agrees with the canonical fibre comparison $Y_s\simeq P_q(s)$ induced by the cone adjunction. For maps of right fibrations, evaluation of the resulting transformation at $s$ agrees with the map of their Kan fibres, including simplicial parameters. The comparisons are natural for maps of right fibrations and base pullback; on projective diagrams, base restriction is followed by cofibrant-fibrant replacement when needed.

There is also the following compatibility with the canonical rigidification model of the coherent Hom bifunctor $H_C$ of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]: use the actual pairing of [def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda], whose value at $(a,b)$ is $\operatorname{Sing}|\mathfrak C[C](a,b)|$, with its specified precomposition and postcomposition action. Right-pinched mapping spaces are compared with this model by the natural pinched-rigidification and singular-realization equivalences. For every $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory $C$, vertex $c\in C$, and coherent functor $v:S\to C$, put $q_{v,c}:S\times_C C_{/c}\to S$, where $(C_{/c})_n$ is the set of maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to C$ with last vertex $c$ and the projection restricts to the initial face. There is a coherent natural equivalence
$$\Phi_S(q_{v,c})\simeq H_C(v(-),c)$$
in $\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$. At a vertex this equivalence uses the canonical right-pinched mapping-space comparison with the rigidification Hom pairing; it preserves the underlying edge $v(s)\to c$. It compares the actions and every higher simplex of these two specified functors, rather than only their values or homotopy classes of edge actions. This equivalence is coherent in $v,c$ and functors of $C$, and compatible with the preceding fibre-evaluation comparison. Empty bases and empty fibres are allowed.

source.place: Agent-formulated compatibility theorem for the specific evaluation and ordered-cone models: Section 2.2.1 and Proposition 2.2.3.11 (cone adjunction), Proposition 2.2.3.15 (fibre comparison), Proposition A.3.4.13 and Corollary A.3.4.14 (enriched evaluation), and Section 5.1.3 (coherent Hom pairing). These sources do not state this combined compatibility verbatim. Online HTT read; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: First explain how to pass the independent enriched statements below to coherent nerves. For locally Kan $A$ there is a natural identity $\operatorname{Map}^R_{N_{\mathrm{hc}}A}(a,b)=\operatorname{Sing}_Q A(a,b)$: by adjunction, a right-pinched $n$-simplex is a functor $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to A$, and its only nonidentity datum is $Q^n\to A(a,b)$. The maps $p_{\operatorname{Sing}_Q T}$ and $e_T$ in [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution] give a natural weak-equivalence zigzag between this mapping space and $T=A(a,b)$. Thus a Dwyer--Kan equivalence between locally Kan categories induces equivalences on all nerve mapping spaces. Their homotopy categories are the path-component categories: edges are enriched vertices, and a triangle gives a path between the long edge and the enriched composite, since $\mathfrak C[\Delta^2](0,2)=\Delta^1$. Conversely each such path supplies that triangle. Hence the induced nerve functor is also essentially surjective. Both nerves are quasicategories by [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to its full essential image, which contains every vertex and consequently every simplex. This supplies a coherent inverse. This argument uses no general coherent-nerve comparison theorem.

source.place: Section 2.2.4, the $Q$-resolution mapping comparison; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak C\dashv N$ for the actual simplex-colimit adjunction: maps out of the colimit $\mathfrak C[K]$ are precisely compatible enriched functors on all simplices of $K$, hence simplicial maps $K\to N(A)$. By [lem-coef-rigidification-boundary-cube], $\mathfrak C$ sends a boundary inclusion to a free enriched cube-boundary cofibration; decomposing a monomorphism by its nondegenerate simplices therefore shows that it preserves cofibrations. In particular every $\mathfrak C[K]$ is cofibrant. By [lem-coef-rigidification-equivalence-detection], it preserves Joyal weak equivalences. These two assertions make this adjunction Quillen for the Joyal and Dwyer--Kan model structures named in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] and [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. For locally Kan $A$ the counit $\epsilon_A:\mathfrak C[NA]\to A$ is Dwyer--Kan. Indeed it fixes objects, and on each mapping set the composite $|\operatorname{Map}^R_{NA}(a,b)|_Q\xrightarrow{\theta}\mathfrak C[NA](a,b)\xrightarrow{\epsilon_A} A(a,b)$ is exactly $e_{A(a,b)}$ under Step 1's identity: on each $Q^n$ summand both evaluate the same enriched functor. The first and the composite maps are weak equivalences by the pinched-resolution statement, so the second is weak by two-out-of-three.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1; direct counit argument from Section 2.2.4; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: For a map $a:\mathfrak C[K]\to A$ with locally Kan target, let $a^\flat:K\to NA$ be its adjoint. The triangle identity gives $a=\epsilon_A\mathfrak C[a^\flat]$. By Step 2 and rigidification equivalence detection, $a$ is Dwyer--Kan exactly when $a^\flat$ is a categorical equivalence. Thus the cofibrant-to-fibrant test for this Quillen adjunction is an equivalence test. The ordinary derived adjunction exists by [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion]. It is an equivalence: replace a target fibrantly and a source cofibrantly; the derived unit is adjoint to the target replacement and the derived counit is adjoint to the source replacement, so the displayed test makes both weak equivalences. The adjunction on maps modulo homotopy is well defined because either adjoint sends cylinder/path homotopies between these replacements to homotopies; the adjunction bijection then descends. This gives the inverse functors on homotopy categories with these units and counits. We shall only use this ordinary model-homotopy-category equivalence to transfer the weak exponential of Step 7; it is derived here rather than taken from a node depending on this item.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, cofibrant-to-fibrant test and adjunction identities; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: This homotopy-category equivalence preserves products. Compute a derived product of enriched categories on locally Kan replacements: their ordinary product is a homotopy product, and $N(A\times B)=NA\times NB$ degree by degree. On the Joyal side all objects are cofibrant. The pushout-product assertion of [lem-coef-joyal-cartesian-pushout-product] says that $-\times K\dashv\operatorname{Fun}(K,-)$ is Quillen for every $K$. Consequently, for quasicategory $Q$, its actual evaluation induces $[L,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)]_{\mathrm J}=[L\times K,Q]_{\mathrm J}$: apply the ordinary adjunction to cofibrant sources and fibrant targets and then to their homotopies. No replacement of $L$ or $K$ is needed. Products on the enriched side are the derived products in [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. Thus transporting an evaluation span exhibiting a weak exponential through Step 3 gives the actual Joyal exponential comparison, with the same evaluation map. This is just substitution in the two Hom-set bijections, retaining the maps inducing them.

source.place: Remark A.3.6.4; cartesian Joyal adjunction written out; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: Choose a larger universe $\mathcal W$ and put $\mathcal M=\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal W}$, $U=\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}\subset\mathcal M$ and $I=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]$. The isomorphism reverses ordered labels and interval subsets and respects union. Thus $I$ is cofibrant by Step 2. By [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model], $\mathcal M$ is combinatorial in $\mathcal W$, and $U$ is genuinely small there; we do not regard $\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$ as cocomplete for $\mathcal W$-small colimits. The subcategory $U$ is an $I$-chunk. To check its closure, choose enriched generating factorizations in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal M^I$. By [lem-coef-enriched-functorial-factorizations] these exist for boundaries and horns, respectively their free $I$-diagrams: tensoring such a generator with any simplicial $K$ remains a cofibration, respectively trivial cofibration, by the simplicial model lifting axiom. On $\mathcal V$-small input they may be constructed entirely in $\mathcal V$: every attaching family is indexed by a small simplicial mapping set, the free diagrams use the $\mathcal V$-small $I$-homs, and the free generator domains test finitely many simplices at one vertex and so preserve sequential cell unions; the small-object iteration has a regular bound in $\mathcal V$. Finite products, coproducts and their factorizations therefore remain in $U$, including for $I$-diagrams. The same small construction computed in $\mathcal W$ has the same lifting classes on these inputs. It gives the enriched finite-fan and finite-cofan factorizations required by the chunk definition, with all intermediate values in $U$.

source.place: Example A.3.4.4, Notation A.3.4.9; full-category chunk, with bookkeeping universe enlargement; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: Write $A=(\mathsf D_S)^{cf}$ and $B=(U^I)^f$, with the projective structures just checked. Enriched cofibrant replacement within $B$ gives $Q:B\to A$ and a natural trivial fibration $QF\to F$; $QF$ is fibrant since $F$ is. It preserves weak maps by two-out-of-three in that naturality square. Weak maps between objects of $A$ are invertible in $\pi_0 A$: apply [lem-coef-model-cylinder-whitehead] to the good simplicial cylinders $F\otimes\Delta^1$, whose endpoint inclusion is trivial cofibrant by the simplicial model axiom and whose projection is then weak by two-out-of-three, and read the inverse homotopies as paths in the enriched mapping sets. Thus $A\to A[W^{-1}]$ is Dwyer--Kan by [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. The inclusion and $Q$ induce inverse maps between $A[W^{-1}]$ and $B[W^{-1}]$: their composites have the natural weak arrows just displayed. After inversion these natural arrows are homotopies of enriched functors; explicitly use their map from the product with the walking arrow, invert its components, and apply [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-product-parameter] to pass to the localized product. The localization universal property then gives the two inverse equations. Hence $A\simeq B[W^{-1}]=E_U(I)$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$, compatibly with evaluation. Also $U^f=\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$; the same Whitehead argument makes every $W$ already invertible in its path-component category, so $X_U=U^f[W^{-1}]\simeq\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$.

source.place: Lemma A.3.6.17 and the evaluation spans in the proof of Proposition A.3.6.16; explicit replacement inside the small chunk, with enriched localization universal property.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-chunk-localized-evaluation-exponential] to the small $I$-chunk $U$ of Step 5. Localized enriched evaluation exhibits $E_U(I)$ as a weak exponential of $X_U$ by $I$: for every test simplicial category $T$, $[T,E_U(I)]_{\mathrm{DK}}\cong[T\times^h I,X_U]_{\mathrm{DK}}$, with bijection induced by actual evaluation. Step 6 replaces the two localized terms by $\mathsf D_S^{cf}$ and $\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$, preserving that evaluation span. Step 3 sends $I=\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]$ to $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ and sends these locally Kan categories to their actual nerves. Steps 3--4 therefore give, naturally for every simplicial set $L$ in the containing universe,
$$[L,N\mathsf D_S^{cf}]_{\mathrm J}\cong[L\times S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}]_{\mathrm J}\cong[L,\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})]_{\mathrm J}.$$
The inducing map is $\mathsf{ev}_S$: the rigidification unit on $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ and enriched evaluation are exactly its definition. Evaluation of the natural replacements in Step 6 gives objectwise weak-equivalence transformations, hence the same morphism in the homotopy category. All testers now really are small in a containing universe, so the Hom bijection applies also when $L$ is the entire source or target of $\mathsf{ev}_S$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13, Corollary A.3.4.14; evaluation span transferred via Steps 1--4; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: The map $\mathsf{ev}_S$ is an isomorphism in the Joyal homotopy category: in Step 7 take $L$ to be its target to obtain a right inverse, then take $L$ to be its source and use injectivity to obtain the other inverse equation. Its source is a quasicategory, since the simplicial model lifting axiom makes the mapping sets between cofibrant-fibrant objects Kan; apply [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory]. Its target is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Represent the inverse by an actual map using [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective]; use [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] to realize its two inverse equations by homotopies for the following good cylinder. In the Joyal model take the interval $N(\mathbb J)$, where $\mathbb J$ is the two-object groupoid with a unique arrow between any pair: its projection to the point has the displayed categorical inverse and its endpoint inclusion is monomorphic. Products with the source give a cylinder by the cartesian pushout-product theorem. Its homotopies are equivalence edges in the internal functor quasicategory. Thus the inverse equations just obtained give coherent inverse transformations, proving that this particular $\mathsf{ev}_S$ is a functor equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4 / Section A.3.4; equivalence of the specific evaluation, deduced from the preceding Hom bijections; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: Use the canonical enrichment specified in [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent], induced by $Q^n\to\Delta^n$. The resulting enriched $U_S:\mathsf D_S^{cf}\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ is Dwyer--Kan by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Both categories are locally Kan: for the first use its simplicial model axiom; for the second its stated mapping complexes are Kan. Step 1 makes $NU_S$ a functor equivalence. Choose its coherent inverse $V_S$ with the inverse transformations, and define $\Phi_S=\mathsf{ev}_S V_S$. Whiskering $V_SNU_S\simeq1$ gives $\Phi_SNU_S\simeq\mathsf{ev}_S$, and Step 8 and this construction show that $\Phi_S$ is an equivalence. No abstract straightening theorem has been substituted for this specified $U_S$ or this specified evaluation. All subsequent comparisons use the same inverse transformations.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.11 and the explicitly specified enriched $U_S$; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text:
Let $q:Y\to S$ be a right fibration. The slice model makes $Y$ cofibrant and fibrant, and $T$ is left Quillen, so $T_q$ is projectively cofibrant. For the given trivial cofibration $j:T_q\to P_q$ with fibrant target, $P_q$ is therefore cofibrant-fibrant. By the stated Quillen-equivalence test its adjoint $a_q:Y\to U_SP_q$ is a weak equivalence. Both objects are right fibrations. Applying the slice simplicial model axiom, or the fibrewise criterion in the presentation, gives an equivalence in $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$. The representable-times-coend identity of [lem-coef-cone-boundary-projective-cells] identifies the straightening of the fibre over the point with $|Y_s|_Q$. Its fibre adjoint is therefore
$$|Y_s|_Q\longrightarrow T_q(s)\xrightarrow{j_s}P_q(s).$$
Indeed both adjoints restrict an enriched cone map along $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to M_q$ on each $Q^n$ summand. The first map is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-right-straightening-fiber-comparison], and the second is one because $j$ is projectively weak. Adjunction with $|{-}|_Q\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ identifies the fibre map of $a_q$ with $Y_s\to\operatorname{Sing}_Q P_q(s)$. This is precisely the canonical cone-adjunction fibre comparison in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.15 and Remark 2.2.2.11; adjoint fibre map; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text:
We verify the transport comparison for $U_SP$ at the level of the cone formula, with $P$ objectwise Kan. Its fibre at $s$ is $\operatorname{Sing}_Q P(s)$, and $\beta_s:P(s)\to\operatorname{Sing}_Q P(s)$ is induced by $p:Q^m\to\Delta^m$, a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-unstraightening-simplex-pointwise]. Over a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$, the following ordered-subset formula specifies compatible lifts of this family of fibre points. For $i\leq n$, send a subset $B\subseteq\{i,\ldots,n+1\}$ containing $i,n+1$ to
$$r_i(B)=(B\setminus\{n+1\})\cup\{n\}\subseteq\{i,\ldots,n\}.$$
Apply $P$ to the resulting map of enriched mapping cubes and then act on $x\in P(\sigma(n))$. This is an enriched map $T_\sigma\to P$: $r_i(B\cup D)=B\cup r_j(D)$ for a path $B$ from $i$ to $j$ and a cone path $D$ from $j$ to $n+1$. Extend along $\mathfrak C[\sigma]$ by the precomposition action of $P$; the cone pushout gives $T_\sigma\to P$ on the whole base $S$. Its adjoint is the asserted lift over $\sigma$. With a simplicial parameter, use the canonical enrichment of [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent], namely precomposition by $Q^m\to\Delta^m$; its fibre is $\beta_s$. These are actual maps on mapping cubes and parameter simplices.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 cone formula, Remark 2.2.2.12; explicit terminal-subset lift; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text:
Here is why these lifts compare whole diagrams. A chain of endpoint-containing subsets records a simplex of a mapping cube. Applying $P$ to that chain supplies the corresponding coherent action simplex. Union of chains gives composition and singleton endpoint paths give units. If a face retains $n$, the formula in Step 11 restricts literally to that face. If it omits $n$, the inclusion of its endpoint path into the path with $n$ inserted is a simplex of the same subset-poset cube; its image under $P$ is the homotopy between the restricted lift and the lift normalized at the new last vertex. For successive omissions, the nested inserted subsets give the entire higher homotopy, with faces obtained by deleting entries of that chain. Degeneracies repeat entries. Thus all the coherence faces agree, by image-of-subsets functoriality and union, not by a deduction from edge actions. Together with $\beta_s$ these lifts give a coherent transformation
$$\mathsf{ev}_S(P)\longrightarrow m_{U_SP}.$$
Use the transport construction of [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit] with these compatible lift data; its contractible compatible choices identify it with the stipulated $m$. Every component is the weak equivalence $\beta_s$, hence it is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Enriched maps $P\times\Delta^m\to P'$ commute with these formulas, so the transformation is natural including all parameters.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 and Section 3.3.3; subset-chain transport and every coherence face; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text:
Transport is functorial for actual maps of right fibrations: apply such a map to every compatible lift used in its definition. If that map has an inverse and homotopies over the base, the same construction gives inverse transformations of transport functors. Apply this to $a_q$ from Step 10 and then Step 12 to get
$$m_q\simeq m_{U_SP_q}\simeq\mathsf{ev}_S(P_q).$$
Applying $\Phi_S$ to $a_q$, followed by the equivalence of Step 9, also gives $\Phi_S(q)\simeq\mathsf{ev}_S(P_q)$. The fibre of the first comparison is the adjoint map in Step 10 followed by the inverse of $\beta_s$. Hence it is exactly the stated canonical equivalence $Y_s\simeq P_q(s)$. Composition of a map $Y\times\Delta^m\to Y'$ with the adjunction maps restricts at $s$ to the same map of fibres; Step 12's parameter calculation makes this the evaluated transformation. Unit and counit compatibility holds because $a_q$ is the adjoint of $j$, not an independently chosen fibre equivalence: its equation is $a_q=U_S(j)\eta_Y$, and for a diagram the opposite composite is $\epsilon_P T(a)$. The two triangle equations cancel the adjacent unit/counit factors. For two allowed replacements, restriction $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(P_q,P'_q)\to\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(T_q,P'_q)$ is a trivial Kan fibration by the simplicial model axiom. Its fibre over the second replacement map is contractible, and all its vertices are weak equivalences by two-out-of-three. Thus arbitrary replacements give coherently compatible comparisons, rather than unrelated choices.

source.place: Sections 2.2.1--2.2.3; ordinary adjunction identities with replacements inverted; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text:
For the Hom clause let $q:S\times_C C_{/c}\to S$ and $A=\mathfrak C[C]$. This is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Its actual simplices supply a map $M_q\to A$: on $\mathfrak C[S]$ use $\mathfrak C[v]$, send the cone vertex to $c$, and on a simplex of $Y$ with its cone use the very simplex $\Delta^{n+1}\to C$ defining the join slice. The restrictions agree on $\mathfrak C[Y]$, so the pushout defining $M_q$ supplies the map. On mapping sets into the cone vertex it gives an enriched natural augmentation
$$b:T_q\longrightarrow A(v(-),c).$$
Compose with the product-preserving singular-realization enriched unit of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], obtaining $\bar b:T_q\to R_{v,c}$, where $R_{v,c}(s)=\operatorname{Sing}|A(v(s),c)|$ is an objectwise Kan enriched presheaf. The enriched naturality equation is composition in $M_q$ followed by the functor to $A$; the unit preserves that composition. This constructs an actual enriched map, including every mapping simplex.

source.place: Section 2.1.2 join slices, Section 2.2.1 ordered cone, Section 5.1.3 canonical Hom model; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: At $s$, write $M=\operatorname{Map}^R_C(v(s),c)=Y_s$. The composite $|M|_Q\to T_q(s)\xrightarrow{b_s}A(v(s),c)$ is exactly $\theta_{C,v(s),c}$: on a summand $Q^n$ both maps are induced by the same map $J^n\to C$ from the right-pinched simplex. The first arrow is weak by right-straightening fibre comparison, and the composite is weak by pinched-rigidification resolution. Thus $b_s$, and then $\bar b_s$, are weak equivalences; the latter uses the singular-realization unit equivalence of [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. This proves that $\bar b$ is a projective weak equivalence. For an arbitrary $j:T_q\to P_q$, extend $\bar b$ across $j$ into the fibrant diagram $R_{v,c}$. The projective lifting axiom gives an extension $P_q\to R_{v,c}$, weak by two-out-of-three. Evaluation is defined on every objectwise Kan enriched diagram: the action takes values in $\mathbf{Kan}$ and transposes after the rigidification unit. It therefore evaluates this map even though $R_{v,c}$ need not be projectively cofibrant. Its components are weak equivalences of Kan complexes, so enhanced functor calculus makes it an equivalence of coherent diagrams. Its space of extensions is contractible: the simplicial model axiom makes $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(P_q,R_{v,c})\to\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(T_q,R_{v,c})$ a trivial Kan fibration. Thus this extension yields the same coherent comparison for every allowed $P_q$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.15 and Section 2.2.4; augmentation checked on each $Q^n$ summand; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text:
Enriched evaluation of $R_{v,c}$ is literally $H_C(v(-),c)$ in the canonical model specified in the statement. Indeed both take $s$ to $\operatorname{Sing}|A(v(s),c)|$; on a simplex of $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ both apply the reflected ordered-subset paths through $\mathfrak C[v]$ and precompose in $A$, as prescribed in [def-coef-infinity-presheaf-yoneda]. Thus they are the same simplicial map, not diagrams identified from vertex values. Combining Steps 9--10 and 14--15 gives
$$\Phi_S(q)\simeq\mathsf{ev}_S(P_q)\simeq H_C(v(-),c).$$
Its fibre comparison is the canonical zigzag $M\leftarrow|M|_Q\xrightarrow{\theta}A(v(s),c)\to\operatorname{Sing}|A(v(s),c)|$, by the summand calculation in Step 15. Degree zero has $Q^0=\Delta^0$, so this sends each point to its own edge $v(s)\to c$. For an enriched parameter the same equation holds on every $Q^n$ summand. This proves the specific mapping comparison and its agreement with the fibre-evaluation comparison, as well as preservation of the underlying edge.

source.place: Section 5.1.3; explicit reflected-subset definition of the canonical Hom pairing; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: For $u:B\to S$, the presentation gives $u^*U_SP=U_B(P\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}})$. Evaluation commutes with restriction by its definition. Restriction may destroy projective cofibrancy, so insert an enriched cofibrant replacement of that objectwise Kan diagram. It stays fibrant, its objectwise weak equivalence evaluates to a pointwise equivalence, and $U_B$ carries it to an equivalence. Pasting this square with the chosen inverse transformations of $NU_B$ and $NU_S$ defines $u^*\Phi_S\simeq\Phi_Bu^*$. To obtain all composition simplices simultaneously, invert the component equivalences of the transformation $NU$ in the functor quasicategory of these restriction diagrams; componentwise equivalences are equivalences by enhanced functor calculus. Equivalently each iterated pasted square inserts the same $VNU\simeq1$ at each intermediate base, and the inverse transformations' simplices give its faces and degeneracies. Thus the comparison is coherent in base maps. Maps of right fibrations act on all lift simplices in Steps 11--13, and maps of $v$ with fixed target act by base restriction. This proves those naturalities without choosing new inverses at separate vertices.

source.place: Naturality of the cone adjunction and enriched evaluation; Sections 2.2.1, 5.1.3; agent argument using the cited DAG statements, not a quotation of a combined compatibility theorem.

proof.text: For coherence in the target $c$, work first with $S=C,v=1$. Use the universal arrow-cone geometry of [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-join-geometry] with its full subcategory equal to $C$. It gives $K=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$, target $u:K\to C$, and one evaluation map $G:K\star_C C\to C$. Its restriction along $(C_{/c})^\triangleright\to K\star_C C$ is exactly the join-slice augmentation of Step 14. Here $K_c\to C$ by source is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration]. The slice diagonal $C_{/c}\to K_c$ is source-preserving and an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]; [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] and the presentation make it a fibrewise equivalence, preserved by source pullback along $v$. Target transport is postcomposition: over $d:c\to c\prime$ use the arrow square from $e:x\to c$ to $de:x\to c\prime$ with source side $1_x$ and target side $d$. Its mixed triangle is evaluated by $G$ as composition. The family thus represents the required slices over the source base. Apply rigidification and the enriched singular-realization unit to $G$. On every mixed simplex of the relative join this gives composition into the varying apex; at fixed $c$ it is $\bar b$ from Step 14. The relative-join operators are $(z,(\epsilon,\sigma))\mapsto(\alpha^*z,(\epsilon\alpha,\alpha^*\sigma))$ by [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. Consequently these augmentations commute with every target-parameter face and degeneracy. In the canonical Hom model the same simplex acts by postcomposition at the apex, so the augmentation compares the entire target-varying diagrams. Pullback along $v$ gives the claim for general $S$. A functor $C\to C'$ acts on these arrow prisms, relative joins and coned simplices; naturality of rigidification and its enriched unit gives the corresponding comparison on every simplex, as required.

proof.text:
Retain the target parameters of Step 18 through replacement as follows. Choose the enriched fibrant replacement functor $F\mapsto RF$ of [lem-coef-enriched-functorial-factorizations] on projective diagrams, with natural trivial cofibration $i_F:F\to RF$. The augmentation $\bar b:T_q\to R_{v,c}$ gives a natural zigzag of fibrant diagrams
$$RT_q\xrightarrow{R\bar b}R(R_{v,c})\xleftarrow{i_{R_{v,c}}}R_{v,c}.$$
Both arrows are weak: naturality $i_{R_{v,c}}\bar b=(R\bar b)i_{T_q}$ and two-out-of-three prove this. All three diagrams evaluate since they are objectwise Kan. Evaluation of this zigzag is a zigzag of componentwise equivalences, so invert it in the functor quasicategory, retaining its whole parameter diagram by enhanced functor calculus. This gives coherent comparisons, rather than inferring simultaneous choices from contractibility of individual extension fibres. For a separately specified $j:T_q\to P_q$, the restriction map $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(RT_q,P_q)\to\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(T_q,P_q)$ is a trivial Kan fibration by the projective simplicial model axiom. Its fibre over $j$ is contractible and every extension is weak by two-out-of-three. It identifies this chosen replacement with the preceding functorial comparison, with all compatible homotopies. For a fixed replacement the extension space in Step 15 gives the same comparison. Therefore the coherent target/functor/base comparisons and all the arbitrary-replacement fibre comparisons belong to one construction.
